findings.finding: The Gerrit hook chaining mechanism has a silent-failure ordering gap: pre-commit's migration mode only preserves an existing `commit-msg` as `.legacy` when the file is present at the moment `pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg` runs. CONTRIBUTING.md §1b tells developers to `curl -Lo .git/hooks/commit-msg` as a separate step, and `make install` / `make hooks` does not enforce any ordering. If a developer runs `make hooks` (or `make install`) before fetching Gerrit's hook, pre-commit writes its own commit-msg hook with no legacy to chain; when the developer then fetches Gerrit's hook via `curl -Lo .git/hooks/commit-msg`, that curl silently overwrites pre-commit's commit-msg hook, deleting the wrap-72 gate entirely — no error, no warning. The plan says Gerrit's hook absence 'must not block wiring the local gates' but does not specify any detection or recovery path for the reverse scenario (Gerrit hook installed AFTER pre-commit's commit-msg hook).

findings.finding: The Gerrit hook chaining mechanism has a silent-failure ordering gap: pre-commit's migration mode only preserves an existing `commit-msg` as `.legacy` — if `make hooks`/`make install` runs BEFORE Gerrit's commit-msg hook is curl-installed (e.g., a developer clones and runs `make install` first, or `make worktree` provisions a fresh clone), pre-commit installs its commit-msg shim with nothing to chain, and all subsequent commits silently lack a Change-Id, breaking every Gerrit push. The plan names `make hooks` as the guard but does not specify what it does when the Gerrit hook slot is absent at install time, nor does it guard against this ordering in `make worktree` (which calls `make install`).
findings.location: Approach section — 'Critical risk handled: Gerrit's commit-msg hook'; AC: 'make hooks verifies both hook types AND that Change-Id stamping survives'
findings.suggested_fix: In the `make hooks` target, add a pre-install check: if `.git/hooks/commit-msg` does not exist (or does not contain Gerrit's hook), print an explicit error — 'Gerrit commit-msg hook not installed; run the curl install from CONTRIBUTING.md §1b first' — and exit non-zero before running `pre-commit install`. This prevents silent slot capture and makes the ordering explicit and enforced.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add test cases for non-ASCII input (CJK wide characters, combining diacritics) to the unit test plan, and specify whether the checker measures codepoint count or terminal column width (e.g. via `wcwidth`/`unicodedata.east_asian_width`) so the behavior is intentional and tested.
evidence: The AC list names carve-outs (URLs, paths, trailers, fenced blocks) but never mentions non-ASCII or multibyte input handling.
The context section cites Go, Chromium, ChromiumOS, and Android projects — all of which receive commits in non-Latin scripts.
Python `len('中文')` == 2, but these two characters occupy 4 terminal columns — a 36-CJK-character line is 72 terminal columns but `len()` == 36, so it would pass the check incorrectly.
ABSENCE: no mention of `wcwidth`, `unicodedata.east_asian_width`, or any multibyte-aware column-counting in the plan.
findings.finding: The testing plan never addresses multibyte / non-Latin input (CJK wide characters, combining diacritics, RTL scripts) for the line-length checker. A checker that enforces a 72-column rule using Python's `len()` (which counts Unicode codepoints, not terminal column widths) will silently under-flag over-long CJK lines (each CJK character is 2 terminal columns) and may miscount combining-character sequences, producing both false negatives and false positives for non-ASCII commit messages — an uncovered failure path for a new user-facing enforcement tool.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Unit tests cover the rule, every carve-out, the fence-toggle case, and the CLI exit codes' / scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py
scenarios: A contributor submits a commit with a CJK body line that is 37 characters (74 terminal columns); the checker passes it when it should reject it.
A line with combining diacritics is miscounted in the opposite direction, producing a false positive rejection of a conforming commit.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide on the column-counting semantic (e.g., use `wcswidth` / `unicodedata.east_asian_width` for terminal-column count) and add AC + unit tests for: (a) a CJK line at exactly 72 terminal columns (pass), (b) a CJK line at 73 terminal columns (reject), (c) a combining-diacritic-heavy line (pass), (d) an empty non-ASCII line (pass). Document the chosen semantic in the checker's module docstring.
